properties.content:

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: APAC MISSOURI INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 0 gallons
0N 9/18 A >100 YEAR RAINFALL EVENT OCCURRED CAUSING LOW WATER CROSSING OF SCOTTS BRANCH (INTERMITTENT STREAM) TO WASH OUT. APAC (SUBCONTRACTOR WORKING ON BRIDGE) HAD A CRANE ON SITE WHICH TIPPED INTO THE WATER WHEN THE CROSSING WASHED OUT. PERSONNEL ON SITE DID NOT OBSERVE ANY SHEEN OR DISCHARGE OF FUELS OR OIL. ON 9/20 WATER WAS SUBSTANTIALLY LOWER. BOOMS WERE DEPLOYED DOWN STREAM AND THE CRANE REMOVED. AFTER REMOVAL, THE FLUID LEVELS OF THE RADIATOR, FUEL TANK, AND CRANK CASE WERE IMMEDIATELY OBSERVED AND APPEARED TO BE AT NORMAL OPERATING LEVELS. NO RELEASE APPEARS TO HAVE TAKEN PLACE AND ON SITE PERSONNEL NEVER OBSERVED ANY VISIBLE SHEEN ON THE WATER. ON 9/21 THE COMPANY WAS INFORMED THAT THE PRIME CONTRACTOR (KTU) DID INDEED NOTICE A SLIGHT SHEEN VISIBLE AGAINST ONE OF THE BOOMS ON 9/20. WHEN PROVIDED WITH THIS INFORMATION, APAC CHOSE TO CALL AND REPORT THE INCIDENT. CURRENTLY THE CRANE IS OUT OF THE WATER, THE BOOMS HAVE BEEN REMOVED, THE WATER LEVEL HAS SUBSIDED AND THERE IS NO EVIDENCE OF ANY SHEEN AT THE LOCATION OR DOWNSTREAM.

properties.content:
Report Details

Nearest City: Jacksonville, FL
Incident Type: MOBILE

Medium Affected: WATER

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 30.330165, -81.654750 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 25 gallons
Report Description
*****CORRECTION TO INITIAL WEB REPORT 993085*****M/V ALBATROSS IV ALONGSIDE LAYBERTH AT NORTH FLORIDA SHIPYARDS, JACKSONVILLE, FL. RECEIVING DIESEL FUEL DELIVERY/TRANSFER FROM 2 SHORESIDE TANK TRUCKS. DECLARATION OF SECURITY AND FUEL TRANSFER PROCEDURES WERE AGREED UPON, CHIEF ENGR ON DUTY WITH 4 CREWMEMBERS STANDING BY ASSISTING. IT WAS OBSERVED THAT FUEL BEGAN TO LEAK OUT OF ONE OF THE TRUCKS AND OPERATIONS WERE IMMEDIATELY SHUTDOWN. CONTAINMENT ABSORBENT PADS WERE RUN OUT AND A SMALL AMOUNT OF DIESEL DROOLED OVER THE EDGE OF THE DOCK INTO THE ST. JOHNS RIVER (APPROX 5GALS) IN MY ESTIMATION THE ENTIRE SPILL WAS APPROX. 20-25 GALS. TOTAL. THE FACT THAT THE ABSORBENT PADS AND BOOM WERE AVAILABLE KEPT IT FROM REACHING THE WATER IN GREATER VOLUME. I WAS UP IN THE VESSELS WHEELHOUSE AND BECAME AWARE OF THE INCIDENT @ APPROX 1730 EDST. AFTER MAKING CERTAIN THAT ALL TRANSFER OPERATIONS WERE SHUTDOWN AND WOULD NOT CONTINUE, I REPORTED THIS INCIDENT TO JACKSONVILLE USCG SECTOR AND WAS TRANSFERRED TO NRC

READINGS ALL CLEAR AT OTHER LOCATIONS. 3 PEOPLE HOSPITALIZED, 1 HELD OVER NIGHT FOR OBSERVATION, 2 RELEASED.

Suspected Responsible Party: TRANSOCEAN OFFSHORE DEEPWATER DRILLING
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 27.225000, -89.995000 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 3 gallons
Report Description
AT 2245 ON 11/25/12 THE SUBSEA ENGINEER WAS LOWERING THE BOP ELEVATOR IN PREPARATION TO CAPTURE THE BOP, WHEN A ½ INCH HYDRAULIC HOSE FAILED AT THE FITTING RIGHT AT THE CRIMP ALLOWING A FINE MIST OF BIO BAR 46 TO DISCHARGE ONTO THE 750 TON CART AND SPILLING AN ESTIMATED 3 GALLONS WHICH WAS CONTAINED ON THE DECK, WITH LESS THEN A GALLON POSSIBLY REACHING THE SEA FROM FINE MIST. THE HOSE THAT FAILED WAS THE BOP ELEVATOR JUMPER HOSE FROM THE RING MAIN TO THE DRAG CHAIN LOCATED FORWARD UPPER MOONPOOL DECK LEVEL. THE HYDRAULICS WAS IMMEDIATELY TURNED OFF TO THE BOP ELEVATOR HOSE REMOVED AND REPLACED WITH A NEW ONE AND 750 TON CART AND DECK CLEANED UTILIZING OIL ABSORBENT PADS.

Report DescriptionNOAA/NESDIS MSPR ISSUED POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 06-11-2024 REPORT TIME: 0130 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: N/A IMAGE DATE: 06-10-2024 IMAGE TIME: 1629 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL2A MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 10 METER LOCATION: 29°41"43" N/88°51"02" W AREA: 11.69 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY WAS FOUND NEAR THE CHANDELEUR AREA OF THE GULF OF MEXICO, JUST SE OF BRETON NATIONAL WILDLIFE REFUGE OFF THE LOUISIANA COAST. THE ANOMALY SPANNED AN AREA APPROXIMATELY 4.8NM BY 3.4NM. THE ANOMALY APPEARED TO BE CONNECTED TO SOME BIOGENIC MATERIAL, SO THE FULL EXTENT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED. THAT BEING SAID, THERE WERE POCKETS OF BRIGHTER SHEEN, WHICH MAY HAVE INDICATED RELATIVELY THICKER OIL. THERE WERE NOT MANY OIL FACILITIES IN THE AREA. ALTHOUGH, DUE TO THE APPEARANCE OF THE ANOMALY, OUR CONFIDENCE IS MEDIUM-HIGH. WINDS AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGERY WERE W/WNW AT ~5KTS, WHICH ROUGHLY ALIGNED WITH SOME POSSIBLE FEATHERING FEATURES. UNCERTAINTIES: THERE WERE PLENTY OF FALSE POSITIVES IN THE AREA AND A POINT SOURCE COULD NOT BE IDENTIFIED. THERE WERE ALSO NO KNOWN REPORTS OF POSSIBLE OIL IN THIS AREA AT THE TIME.

TRYING TO FIX IT DOESN'T CUT IT AFTER TEN SPILLS SO WE CAN'T FISH, SWIM, HAVE TO BREATHE DIESEL FUMES AND LOOK FORWARD TO CLEANING DIESEL OFF MY GIRLFRIEND'S SKI BOAT WATERLINE AGAIN. THERE ARE SOLUTIONS FOR DIESEL LEAKS, AND OWNER ISN'T TAKING THIS PROBLEM SERIOUSLY. I HOPE YOU CAN PROVIDE SOME INCENTIVE TO GET HIM TO STOP SPILLING DIESEL FUEL INTO BLUE SPRINGS MARINA'S WATERS. THANK YOU.
